questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.stem: A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours at a constant speed. At this rate, how many miles will it travel in 5 hours?
questions.rationale: The speed is $\frac{180}{3} = 60$ miles per hour. In 5 hours the car travels $60 \times 5 = 300$ miles.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.stem: What is the median of the data set 4, 7, 9, 12, 15?
questions.rationale: The values are already in order and there are 5 of them, so the median is the third value, 9.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red marbles and 15 blue marbles. If one marble is selected at random, what is the probability that it is red?
questions.rationale: There are $5 + 15 = 20$ marbles total, of which 5 are red, so the probability is $\frac{5}{20} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.stem: The ratio of cats to dogs at a shelter is 3 to 5. If there are 15 cats, how many dogs are there?
A shirt originally priced at \$40 is on sale for \$30. What is the percent decrease in price?
questions.rationale: The decrease is $40 - 30 = 10$ dollars. As a percent of the original: $\frac{10}{40} = 0.25$, or 25%.

questions.stimulus: A line of best fit for a scatterplot relating study hours $h$ to exam score $s$ is given by $s = 6.5h + 52$.
questions.stem: According to the model, what is the predicted increase in exam score for each additional hour studied?
questions.rationale: In a linear model, the slope gives the change in the predicted output per one-unit increase in the input. Here the slope is 6.5.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.stimulus:
The list below gives the number of books read by each of 6 students in one month.

2, 3, 3, 5, 8, 15
questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares the mean and the median of the data?

choices.text: The mean is less than the median.
The mean is equal to the median.
The mean is greater than the median.

questions.rationale: The mean is $\frac{2+3+3+5+8+15}{6} = \frac{36}{6} = 6$. The median is the average of the third and fourth values: $\frac{3+5}{2} = 4$. Since $6 > 4$, the mean is greater. The value 15 pulls the mean upward.

questions.stem: The population of a town increased by 20% from 2020 to 2021, then decreased by 10% from 2021 to 2022. If the population in 2020 was 5,000, what was the population in 2022?
questions.rationale: After the increase: $5000 \times 1.20 = 6000$. After the decrease: $6000 \times 0.90 = 5400$.

questions.stimulus:
The table shows the results of a survey of 200 people about whether they own a bicycle.

| | Owns bicycle | Does not own | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under 30 | 60 | 40 | 100 |
| 30 or older | 30 | 70 | 100 |
| Total | 90 | 110 | 200 |
questions.stem: If a person who owns a bicycle is selected at random, what is the probability that the person is under 30?
questions.rationale: The selection is restricted to bicycle owners, of whom there are 90. Of those, 60 are under 30, so the conditional probability is $\frac{60}{90}$.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.stem: A machine produces 45 parts every 4 minutes. At this rate, how many parts does it produce in one hour?
questions.rationale: In 60 minutes there are $\frac{60}{4} = 15$ four-minute intervals. The machine produces $45 \times 15 = 675$ parts.

questions.skill: Inference from sample statistics and margin of error
questions.stimulus: A random sample of 400 residents of a city found that 62% support a proposed park, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points at the 95% confidence level.
questions.stem: Which conclusion is best supported by these results?

choices.text: Exactly 62% of all city residents support the park.
It is plausible that between 58% and 66% of all city residents support the park.
All residents of the city support the park.
Fewer than half of city residents support the park.

questions.rationale: The margin of error creates an interval of $62\% \pm 4\%$, or 58% to 66%. A sample statistic estimates the population value within that interval rather than determining it exactly.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.stem: Which statement about the two data sets is true?

choices.text: The sets have the same mean and the same standard deviation.
The sets have the same mean, but set B has the larger standard deviation.
The sets have the same mean, but set A has the larger standard deviation.
Set B has both the larger mean and the larger standard deviation.

questions.rationale: Both sets have mean 14 and median 14. Set B's values are spread much further from the mean than set A's, so set B has the larger standard deviation.

questions.stem: After a 25% discount, the sale price of an item is \$96. What was the original price?
questions.rationale: A 25% discount means the sale price is 75% of the original: $0.75p = 96$, so $p = \frac{96}{0.75} = 128$.

questions.stimulus: A researcher surveyed visitors leaving a gym and found that 85% reported exercising at least four times per week. The researcher concluded that 85% of all adults in the city exercise at least four times per week.
questions.stem: Which criticism of the conclusion is most valid?

choices.text: The sample size was too small to draw any conclusion.
The sample was not randomly selected from the population of interest.
The survey should have asked about diet as well.
Percentages cannot be used to describe populations.

questions.rationale: People leaving a gym are far more likely to exercise frequently than the general adult population. Because the sample was not drawn randomly from all adults in the city, it cannot support a conclusion about that population.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.stem: A recipe requires 3 cups of flour for every 4 cups of milk. If a baker uses 18 cups of flour, how many cups of milk are needed?
questions.rationale: Set up the proportion $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{18}{m}$. Cross-multiplying gives $3m = 72$, so $m = 24$.

questions.stimulus: A box contains 4 green, 6 yellow, and 10 white tokens.
questions.stem: If one token is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is not white? Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.rationale: There are $4 + 6 + 10 = 20$ tokens, of which $4 + 6 = 10$ are not white. The probability is $\frac{10}{20} = 0.5$.

questions.stimulus: A quantity $y$ decreases exponentially over time $t$, halving every 6 years. At $t = 0$, $y = 800$.
questions.stem: Which expression gives the value of $y$ after $t$ years?
questions.rationale: The quantity is multiplied by 0.5 once every 6 years, and $\frac{t}{6}$ counts how many such periods have elapsed, giving $800(0.5)^{t/6}$.
